agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

"UNIX's missing `loop` command!"

loop lets you write powerful, intuitive looping one-liners in your shell. It provides easy-to-use options
for repeating commands with timers, counters, and stop conditions.

Usage (examples):

- Run a command repeatedly until interrupted:

    $ loop 'echo hello'

- Run a command every 5 seconds:

    $ loop --every 5s -- date

- Stop when output contains a value:

    $ loop --until-contains 200 -- ./get_response_code.sh --site example.com

- Iterate over a list from stdin:

    $ cat items.txt | loop -- 'echo $ITEM'

For more examples and usage patterns, consult the project website or built-in help (if available).

echo "=== for behavior len exceed ==="
timeout 1 ./executable --for a,b -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM COUNT=\$COUNT ACTUALCOUNT=\$ACTUALCOUNT" 2>&1
timeout 1 ./executable --for a,b -n 5 -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM COUNT=\$COUNT" 2>&1

echo "exit:$?"

echo "exit:$?"

echo "=== until-match ==="

echo "=== summary ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --summary -- "bash -c 'if [ \$COUNT -eq 1 ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi; echo hi'" 2>&1

echo "=== only-last ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -l -- "echo hi\$COUNT" 2>&1

echo "=== until-success / fail ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -s -- "bash -c 'echo hi\$COUNT; if [ \$COUNT -eq 2 ]; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi'" 2>&1
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -f -- "bash -c 'echo hi\$COUNT; if [ \$COUNT -eq 3 ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi'" 2>&1
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -r 2 -- "bash -c 'echo hi\$COUNT; if [ \$COUNT -eq 2 ]; then exit 2; else exit 0; fi'" 2>&1

echo "=== offset & count-by negative etc ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -o -5 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -b -1 -o 5 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -b 0 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1

echo "=== until-time ==="
FUTURE=$(date -u -d "+1 seconds" +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" 2>/dev/null || date -u -v+1S +"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" 2>/dev/null || echo "2026-01-01 00:00:00")
echo "future $FUTURE"
timeout 3 ./executable --until-time "$FUTURE" -- "echo hi; date -u +%H:%M:%S" 2>&1 | head -n 20
echo "exit until-time:$?"

echo "=== stdin vs for ==="
printf "s1\ns2\n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -- "echo SITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1
timeout 1 ./executable --for f1,f2 -- "echo FITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1

echo "=== command without -- ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 2 echo hello 2>&1

echo "=== help version ==="
./executable --version 2>&1
./executable --help 2>&1 | head -n 30

EOS
chmod +x /tmp/quick.sh
timeout 50 bash /tmp/quick.sh 2>&1
"}

# until-error

  timeout 2 ./executable "$@" > /tmp/stdout.txt 2> /tmp/stderr.txt
  rc=$?
  echo "rc=$rc"
  echo "stdout:"
  cat /tmp/stdout.txt | sed -n '1,200p' | od -c | head -n 5
  echo "stderr:"
  cat /tmp/stderr.txt | sed -n '1,200p' | od -c | head -n 5
  echo "stdout cat:"
  cat /tmp/stdout.txt | head -n 20 | cat -A
  echo "stderr cat:"
  cat /tmp/stderr.txt | head -n 20 | cat -A
  echo "-----"
}

# 1. COUNT float handling more
echo "=== COUNT floats detailed ==="
for off in 0 0.5 1.5 -0.5; do
  for by in 1 0.5 1.2 0; do
    echo "off=$off by=$by"
    timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --offset "$off" --count-by "$by" -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' '; echo
  done
done

echo "=== COUNT integer vs float formatting ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 2 --offset 0 --count-by 1 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 2 --offset 0.0 --count-by 1 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 2 --offset 0 --count-by 1.0 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 2 --offset 0.00 --count-by 0.00 -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c

# 2. every parsing valid values
echo "=== every valid ==="
for e in 1us 1ms 1s 1m 1h 1h2m3s 5s 500ms 1h1m1s1ms1us "1s " " 1s"; do
  echo "every=$e"
  timeout 1 ./executable -n 1 --every "$e" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo "rc:$? err:$(cat /tmp/err.txt)"
done

# every invalid
for e in "" "abc" "5" "s" "1x" "1h 2s" "1.5s"; do
  echo "every invalid=$e"
  timeout 1 ./executable -n 1 --every "$e" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo "rc:$? err:$(cat /tmp/err.txt)"
done

# 3. for-duration valid/invalid
for d in 1s 500ms 1h2m 0s; do
  timeout 1 ./executable --for-duration "$d" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo "for-d $d rc:$? lines:$(wc -l < /tmp/out.txt) err:$(cat /tmp/err.txt)"
done
for d in "" "abc" "5" "1x"; do
  timeout 1 ./executable --for-duration "$d" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo "invalid for-d $d rc:$? err:$(cat /tmp/err.txt)"
done

# 4. until-time parsing
echo "=== until-time ==="
for t in "2018-04-20 04:20:00" "2026-09-06 12:00:00" "invalid" "" "2018-04-20T04:20:00" "2018-04-20"; do
  timeout 1 ./executable --until-time "$t" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; echo "t=$t rc:$? err:$(cat /tmp/err.txt) out_lines:$(wc -l < /tmp/out.txt)"
done

# 5. until-contains and match with empty, etc
echo "=== until-contains ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -c "" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; echo "c empty rc:$? out:"; cat /tmp/out.txt | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -c "hi" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/out.txt | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -c "notfound" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/out.txt | od -c

# until-match regex
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -m ".*" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/out.txt | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -m "^hi$" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/out.txt | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -m "[" -- "echo hi" > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/err.txt; echo rc:$?

# 6. stdin handling
echo "=== stdin ==="
printf "a\nb\n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM COUNT=\$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c
printf "a\nb\n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -n 1 -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
printf "a\nb\n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -n 5 -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM COUNT=\$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c
printf "" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -n 2 -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c; echo "empty with n=2 rc:$?"
printf "" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -- "echo hi" 2>&1 | timeout 1 head; echo "empty no n rc:$?"
# stdin with spaces and empty lines
printf "a\n\nc\n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -- "echo ITEM=[\$ITEM]" 2>&1 | od -c
printf "  spaces  \n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -- "echo ITEM=[\$ITEM]" 2>&1 | od -c

# 7. for handling
echo "=== for ==="
timeout 1 ./executable --for a,b,c -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable --for a,b,c -n 5 -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable --for a,b -n 3 -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable --for single -- "echo ITEM=\$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable --for "" -- "echo ITEM=[\$ITEM]" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable --for "a, b, c" -- "echo ITEM=[\$ITEM]" 2>&1 | od -c # note spaces after comma
timeout 1 ./executable --for "a,,b" -- "echo ITEM=[\$ITEM]" 2>&1 | od -c

# 8. only-last and summary
echo "=== only-last ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -l -- "echo \$COUNT" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable --for a,b,c -l -- "echo \$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
printf "a\nb\nc\n" | timeout 1 ./executable -i -l -- "echo \$ITEM" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -l --summary -- "echo hi" 2>&1 | od -c

# summary
echo "=== summary ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --summary -- "bash -c 'exit 0'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --summary -- "bash -c 'exit 1'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --summary -- "bash -c 'if [ \$COUNT -eq 1 ]; then exit 0; else exit 2; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --summary -- "echo hi" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 --summary -l -- "echo hi" 2>&1 | od -c

# 9. until-success/fail/error with output
echo "=== until success etc ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -s -- "bash -c 'echo hi\$COUNT; if [ \$COUNT -eq 2 ]; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -f -- "bash -c 'echo hi\$COUNT; if [ \$COUNT -eq 2 ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -r 5 -- "bash -c 'echo hi\$COUNT; if [ \$COUNT -eq 2 ]; then exit 5; else exit 1; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
# test that until-success stops immediately if first success
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -s -- "bash -c 'exit 0'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 5 -f -- "bash -c 'exit 0'" 2>&1 | od -c
# test no success case runs all?
timeout 1 ./executable -n 3 -s -- "bash -c 'exit 1'" 2>&1 | od -c

# 10. until-changes / same
echo "=== until changes/same ==="
timeout 1 ./executable -n 10 -C -- "bash -c 'if [ \$COUNT -lt 2 ]; then echo a; else echo b; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 10 -C -- "echo hi" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 10 -S -- "bash -c 'if [ \$COUNT -lt 2 ]; then echo same; else echo diff; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 10 -S -- "echo hi" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 10 -S -- "bash -c 'if [ \$COUNT -eq 0 ]; then echo a; elif [ \$COUNT -eq 1 ]; then echo b; else echo a; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c
timeout 1 ./executable -n 10 -S -- "bash -c 'if [ \$COUNT -eq 0 ]; then echo a; elif [ \$COUNT -eq 1 ]; then echo b; elif [ \$COUNT -eq 2 ]; then echo b; else echo c; fi'" 2>&1 | od -c

EOS
chmod +x /tmp/brute.sh
timeout 120 bash /tmp/brute.sh 2>&1 | head -n 2500
"}

loop

"UNIX's missing `loop` command!"

loop lets you write powerful, intuitive looping one-liners in your shell. It provides easy-to-use options
for repeating commands with timers, counters, and stop conditions.

Usage (examples):

- Run a command repeatedly until interrupted:

    $ loop 'echo hello'

- Run a command every 5 seconds:

    $ loop --every 5s -- date

- Stop when output contains a value:

    $ loop --until-contains 200 -- ./get_response_code.sh --site example.com

- Iterate over a list from stdin:

    $ cat items.txt | loop -- 'echo $ITEM'

For more examples and usage patterns, consult the project website or built-in help (if available).

License: see the repository LICENSE file.
